title: Compound symmetry and the design effect
title_html: Compound symmetry and the design effect
html:
Let @eq-cls-compound hold with mg=m for all g, let λw=σ2{1+(m−1)ρ} and λs=σ2(1−ρ), and let rank(X)=p.

  1. V=λwPW+λs(I−PW). Its eigenvalues are λw with multiplicity G and λs with multiplicity n−G, and V−1=1λs(I−mρ1+(m−1)ρPW).

  2. C(VX)⊆C(X) iff C(PWX)⊆C(X). In particular, if X=[Xb,Xw] with every column of Xb cluster-constant and every column of Xw cluster-centred, then least squares is generalized least squares and every least squares estimate of an estimable function is best linear unbiased.

  3. Let 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β be estimable and let 𝛌c=X(X⊤X)−λ, so that 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^=c⊤y. If c is cluster-constant then 𝛌𝛃Var(λ⊤β^)={1+(m−1)ρ}⋅σ2‖c‖2, and if c is cluster-centred then 𝛌𝛃Var(λ⊤β^)=(1−ρ)σ2‖c‖2. In both cases σ2‖c‖2 is the variance the estimate would have under 𝛆Cov(ε)=σ2I; the multiplier is the design effect. In either case 𝛌𝛃λ⊤β^ is best linear unbiased even if (b) fails.

  4. Suppose C(X)=Sb⊕Sw with Sb⊆C(PW) of dimension pb and Sw⊆C(PW)⊥ of dimension pw=p−pb. Then the usual residual mean square has E(s2)=λw(G−pb)+λs(n−G−pw)n−p,{#eq-cls-naive-s2}

    and for any c as in (c) the usual variance estimate 𝛌𝛌v=s2λ⊤(X⊤X)−λ satisfies 𝛌𝛃E(v)/Var(λ⊤β^)=E(s2)/λ, with λ=λw or λs according to the stratum of c.
